mission_phase: Generation 28 - WooCommerce inspection engine (slice 1: adapter + catalog/search/browse capture)
phase_goal: Begin a WooCommerce inspection engine paralleling the Shopify path. Slice 1: a WooCommerce Store API adapter + a live capture runner that inspects a Woo store's catalog scale (SKUs, browse nodes/categories, hierarchy levels), submitted search, and category browse, writing honest evidence artifacts. First target: legionathletics.com. Includes the operator-requested catalog summary (SKUs / browse nodes / levels) as a discovery-effort signal.
reason_generation_started: Operator asked to run a full analysis of legionathletics.com and add a catalog summary. Legion is WooCommerce, not Shopify (FND-GEN028-001); the Shopify engine cannot inspect it. Operator chose to build a full WooCommerce inspection engine (multi-generation). This slice lands the adapter + real catalog/search/browse capture; later slices add dashboard site parity, facets/recommendations/rendered capture, a Woo platform capability model, and the shared inspection-report schema.
standing_directive: The operator EXPLICITLY authorized running the Legion analysis this session (lifting the no-auto-run directive for this request). Runs are read-only inspections of the public store via its WooCommerce Store API; be honest about what the API does and does not expose. Do not apply destructive cleanup.

functional: The WooCommerce adapter detects the platform (generator=woocommerce / Store API reachable) and returns catalog scale: total SKUs (products), browse nodes (categories) with parent/child hierarchy and level depth.

The capture runs live against legionathletics.com and produces honest artifacts: a catalog summary (SKUs, browse nodes, levels, top categories, discovery signal), a submitted-search probe (queries -> result counts), and a category browse listing.
Counts reported match the store's Store API (e.g. X-WP-Total for products; categories list length), and the discovery signal is derived, not asserted.
usability: The catalog summary is human-readable and states the discovery signal (small catalog / flat browse -> lower search priority, or the opposite).
Artifacts are inspectable (valid JSON/JSONL) and stored under the Legion assessment directory.
technical: New src/adapters/woocommerce.mjs with unit-checkable methods; the capture writes valid JSON/JSONL; the existing gate (validate:dashboard, validate:gen13, validate) stays green and is not regressed by the new files; git diff --check clean.
